findings.summary: Stage-result contracts have multiple executable owners.
findings.evidence: ground.js:11-31, design.js:23-50, hidden-decision-scan.js:11-58, rule-phase.js:11-36, and tdd.js:11-34 define the producer result shapes and pass them to shared validation. The round-three fix independently re-derives those contracts in refute.js:55-195 and implement.js:36-109. For example, tdd.js:15-33 and 120-129 own testFiles, redProof, coverage, and notes, while implement.js:72-91 separately encodes the same result contract. A producer change can leave its consumer validator stale.
findings.fix: Extract the stage-result schemas and semantic validation into one shared workflow owner, then route both producer acceptance and downstream handoff validation through it. Delete groundOutputProblem, designOutputProblem, hiddenDecisionOutputProblem, rulePhaseResultProblem, and tddResultProblem from the consumers.

The live records lack the canonical fields those branches excuse. contract.md:161-168 limits recovery to this run and says it creates no precedent.
findings.fix: Keep recovery conversion in this run's records or orchestration only. Preserve the original records, produce canonical current GROUND, DESIGN, and RULE-PHASE handoffs, and remove groundResultForRefute, historicalResult, optional success metadata, and caseInsensitiveLens compatibility from reusable workflow code.

findings.fix: Remove tdd from omittedStageAuthorizations and require a TDD result at L1, including the approved no-test result. Retain only the approved L1 RULE-PHASE exception and L2's optional TDD behavior.

Calling IMPLEMENT at L2 without a TDD result is the existing representation that TDD did not run; the IMPLEMENT worker still receives the complete contract and must stop if the contract shows TDD was needed. No approved rule requires a separate TDD-needed result or authorization parameter.
